attribution.note: Zitron's own newsletter. He sums up his earlier argument in his own voice and stands by it.

semantics.note: The normalised claim captures the investment, subsidy and VC elements. The hedged Anthropic subsidy is kept as a qualifier. It describes a present state, so it is an observation.

contract.note: Reading 'subsidizing' as discounted pricing is ordinary. The evidence says the rate was 'substantially reduced', which also fits 'heavily'. The period from 2023 to the post date is reasonable, and leaving out the hedged Anthropic part is correct.

evidence.note: July 2024 secondary summary of The Information. It reports Microsoft's $10B investment in early 2023 and a substantially reduced Azure rate for OpenAI. The wording is hedged ('thought to') and second-hand, but it meets the press-report standard.
Amazon finished its $4B investment in Anthropic in March 2024, inside the target period.
Google committed $2B to Anthropic in October 2023, inside the target period.
Microsoft's filing after the post confirms $13B in total commitments to OpenAI. It backs up the earlier reports but was published after the target period.

reviews.rationale: Multibillion-dollar investments by Microsoft, Amazon and Google in OpenAI and Anthropic during 2023–24 are documented. Press reporting says OpenAI got Azure compute at a substantially reduced rate. That meets the support condition. No counterevidence was found.

attribution.note: Zitron's own newsletter text, in his own voice.

semantics.note: The margin-erosion part uses a firm 'will', so it is scored. The 'I imagine' consequence and the competition assumption are kept and correctly excluded from scoring.

contract.note: 'Begin to' fairly sets a low bar, so one explicit company-attributed case can start the outcome. Counting gross-margin erosion as eating into profitability is an ordinary reading. How many firms 'these companies' requires is still a judgment call.

evidence.note: Figma's CFO said on the Q3 2025 call that the cost of serving AI features hurt gross margin. This is a company disclosure dated after the post and before the evaluation date.
Figma's press release shows non-GAAP gross margin falling from 92% to 86% year on year, a measurable decline tied to AI costs in e1.

reviews.rationale: The early-resolution rule is met. Figma, a public SaaS company, attributed a 6-point gross margin decline in Q3 2025 to the cost of serving generative AI features. The hedged follow-on (price rises or dropping tools) is not scored. Only one company is documented, which is enough for 'begin to'.

semantics.note: The normalised claim keeps 'it feels like' and the 'hundreds of companies' scope. The commoditisation-to-pricing link makes it causal in form, but it is framed as an impression.

contract.note: Treating the sentence as a hedged impression full of value judgments ('death cult', 'mediocre') with no measure is fair. A plain-reading test correctly does not apply to hedged language.

reviews.rationale: The claim is framed as a personal impression ('it feels like') and rests on value judgments with no threshold. It has no firm, testable content, so it is not scored. The case itself is not broken.
